inconsistencies: Soft-fork implementations were banded unevenly when assessed alone: #31989 (CTV) sat at P1 while #32247 (CSFS), #29247 (CAT), #35793 (BIP 54) and #36122 (CISA) sat at P2, despite all being regtest-only or activation-free. All normalized to P2; review #35793 first since it targets known legacy vulnerabilities.

Pruning/BlockManager chain, review in this order: #36735 (base, deferred deletion of pruned files) -> #36738 (moves block writes and pruning into BlockManager, includes #36735 commits) -> #36856 (kernel manual pruning) -> #36857 (kernel prune locks, depends on #36856). #36856 and #36857 each restate the 'move prune bookkeeping out of FlushStateToDisk' change from #36735/#36738; reviewers should confirm the later ones do not duplicate merged or earlier work.
#35861 (Testnet 5) is a direct dependent of #35793 (BIP 54); only its top five commits are new. #35793 must be reviewed and settled first.
#35054 (P2P UTXO set sharing) builds on #36603 (loadtxoutset performance); review #36603 first.

Strategic conflict in the assumeutxo cluster: #36598 demonstrates removing assumeutxo entirely while #36778 (startup-arg loading), #36603 (faster loading), #36543 (commitment checking), #36542, #36500 and #35054 all invest further in it. A direction decision should precede detailed review of the smaller assumeutxo PRs.

#34132, #35003, #36049 and #36799 all change how block/database I/O failures are surfaced (fatal error vs. exception vs. silent stall). They overlap in FlatFileSeq/BlockManager/dbwrapper error paths and should be reviewed as a group to avoid conflicting error-handling conventions.

Validation-state cleanup chain: #35646 (separate runtime errors via util::Expected) unblocks #35570 (return BlockValidationState by value), and #36792 and #36318 fix state-propagation quirks found reviewing #35570. Review order: #35646, #35570, then #36792/#36318.
#34534 (manual prune lock RPCs) and #36857 (kernel prune lock API) expose the same internal prune-lock mechanism at two different layers; they should be reviewed together so the semantics match.
#32427 replaces the LevelDB block tree database entirely, while #35071 persists new reindex-resume state into that same database. Whichever lands first forces rework on the other.

Kernel-API red flag: #35187, #36856, #36857, #35557 and #32427 are primarily libbitcoinkernel API changes that also touch validation persistence or entry points; the validation-behavior parts (block tree storage format, pruning bookkeeping, clock scoping) deserve separately focused review and in some cases splitting.

#35569, #35906 and #36066 are all steps toward the stateless validation library (#35904) but were banded P4/P3/P4; they are ordered here by how much testable validation behavior each actually exposes, not by their shared umbrella.
result.notes: The band distribution is wide on purpose: a small P1 set of crashes, silent corruption and a memory-exhaustion DoS; a large P2 set split between storage/error-handling stability fixes, measured IBD and pruning speedups, and the regtest soft-fork implementations; and a long P3 tail of edge-case fixes and validation-internals cleanups. The main cross-cutting judgment is that regtest-only consensus code and non-mergeable reference implementations rank below fixes that affect running mainnet nodes today, while still staying in P2 because reaching a decision on them is the category's job.
